lessons.title: Renting Out a Home: 11-Month Agreements, Deposits and the Model Tenancy Act

children.text: In parts of South Mumbai, families still live in large flats for a monthly rent of a few hundred rupees, under tenancies that began before Independence. Rent control laws froze those rents and made eviction almost impossible, so owners received nothing close to market rent for generations. That history explains a quirk every Indian landlord now follows: the 11-month rent agreement. This lesson covers why that format exists, what a good agreement must contain, how deposits and disputes really work, and what the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is trying to change.

body.text: Your rent agreement is the only thing standing between a rental income and a legal dispute. Draft it for the day things go wrong, not the day the tenant moves in.

children.text: Why Almost Every Agreement Runs 11 Months

markDefs.definition: Permission to use a property without transferring any interest in it, governed by the Indian Easements Act, 1882. The licensee is an occupant, not a tenant, which makes it easier for the owner to regain possession.

children.text: Under the Registration Act, 1908, a lease for any term exceeding one year must be compulsorily registered, which means paying registration fees and higher stamp duty and visiting the sub-registrar. An 11-month agreement stays below that line in most states. It is also usually drafted as a
rather than a lease, which gives the occupant permission to use the flat without gaining a tenant's stronger rights.

cells: A right to enjoy the property (an interest in it)
Compulsory if the term exceeds one year
Usually avoided by keeping it under 12 months
Can be harder if a dispute arises

body.text: The 11-month trick is not universal. In Maharashtra, all leave and licence agreements must be registered, whatever their length, and the owner bears the responsibility. Registration can be done online. Stamp duty is also payable on rent agreements across states even when registration is not required. An unstamped agreement can be difficult to rely on in court.

children.text: What a Good Agreement Must Contain
Most landlords download a template and fill in names. That works until the tenant stops paying, damages the kitchen or refuses to leave. A well-drafted agreement settles these questions in advance.

body.title: Clauses to Include in Every Residential Agreement
steps: Full names, addresses and PAN of owner and occupant, plus identity proof copies
Monthly rent, due date, payment method and late-payment charge
Security deposit amount, refund timeline and permitted deductions
Term, renewal terms and rent increase on renewal (commonly 5% to 10%)
Lock-in period, if any, and notice period for either side (commonly one to two months)
Who pays society maintenance, utilities and property tax
Split of repairs: day-to-day repairs by occupant, structural repairs by owner
Inventory list of furniture and appliances with their condition, signed by both sides
No sub-letting or change of use without written consent
Owner's right to inspect with advance notice
Handover condition at exit, including painting and cleaning expectations

body.label: Tenant's HRA claim needs your PAN
body.context: Salaried tenants claiming House Rent Allowance exemption must give their employer the landlord's PAN once rent crosses ₹1 lakh a year. Expect the request, and make sure the rent is shown in your own tax return.

children.text: The security deposit is where most landlord-tenant fights happen. Owners hold it as protection against unpaid rent and damage. Tenants treat it as their money, which it is, subject to fair deductions. Common flashpoints are painting charges deducted at exit, disputed damage to fittings, and deposits refunded weeks late.

The cure is documentation. Take dated photos and a video of every room at move-in, attach them to the inventory list, and repeat at exit. Agree in writing whether a standard painting charge will be deducted. Refund promptly, with a written breakdown of deductions. Landlords who do this rarely end up in a dispute, and their flats get recommended to the next tenant.

body.text: A large deposit feels safe, but it can hurt your yield. In a market with plenty of rental supply, a landlord asking for six months when neighbours ask for two will see the flat sit empty longer, and one extra month of vacancy wipes out a year's worth of any "safety" benefit.

children.text: In June 2021, the Union Cabinet approved the Model Tenancy Act to replace the rent control mindset with a balanced, contract-based system. Land and housing are state subjects, so it is a template, not a national law. It applies only where a state enacts its own version. Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Assam are among the states with tenancy laws modelled on or similar to it, while many others still operate under older rent control statutes.

stats.context: In writing, from owner to tenant

markDefs.definition: A district-level officer under the Model Tenancy Act who records tenancy agreements and is the first point of contact for landlord-tenant issues, backed by dedicated Rent Courts and Rent Tribunals.

children.text: Beyond those numbers, the model law requires every tenancy to be in writing and reported to a new

, and sets up Rent Courts and Rent Tribunals meant to settle disputes quickly rather than through years of civil litigation. Non-payment of rent for two consecutive months is a ground for the owner to seek possession. Sub-letting needs the owner's written consent. Importantly, it applies to new tenancies, not to old rent-controlled ones.

body.title: Old rent control vs the Model Tenancy Act approach

columns.label: Old rent control laws
points: Rents frozen or tightly capped for decades
Disputes stuck in civil courts for years
Owners avoid renting or use informal 11-month workarounds
Properties decay because rent cannot fund repairs

columns.label: Model Tenancy Act approach
points: Rent set by agreement between both parties
Clear grounds and process to regain possession
Dedicated Rent Courts and Tribunals with timelines
Written, reported agreements for every tenancy
Deposit caps and repair duties that protect tenants too

body.title: Renting to a company, renting as an NRI, and furnished flats

children.text: Company leases: some employers lease flats directly for staff. You get a stronger payer and often a longer term, but expect the company to deduct TDS and to insist on a registered agreement and clear GST treatment if the flat is used by a business.

NRI owners: if the owner is a non-resident Indian, the tenant must deduct TDS at a much higher rate, around 30% plus surcharge and cess, on rent paid to the NRI. Many tenants do not know this, which creates problems for both sides. NRI landlords should agree on it upfront and use a local power of attorney holder to manage the flat.
Furnished flats: rent is higher, but so are disputes. The inventory list becomes critical, with the brand, model and condition of every appliance recorded.

body.title: Calculate: Overstay Compensation
body.prompt: A tenant in Lucknow paying ₹30,000 a month refuses to vacate when the tenancy ends and stays on for 5 months. Using the Model Tenancy Act framework of double rent for the first two months and four times rent after that, how much compensation is payable, in rupees?
body.explanation: First 2 months: 2 × ₹30,000 × 2 = ₹1,20,000. Next 3 months: 4 × ₹30,000 × 3 = ₹3,60,000. Total: ₹4,80,000. The steep penalty is designed to make overstaying expensive.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Registration Line
body.textWithBlank: Under the Registration Act, 1908, a lease for any term exceeding ___ must be compulsorily registered.
body.explanation: Leases longer than one year must be registered. Keeping agreements at 11 months avoids this in most states, though Maharashtra requires registration of all leave and licence agreements.

body.title: Quick Check: What the Model Act Does
body.question: Which statement about the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is correct?
options: It is a national law that applies automatically in every state
It caps residential security deposits at two months' rent where a state adopts it
It freezes rent on existing old tenancies at current levels
It bans leave and licence agreements
body.explanation: The Model Tenancy Act is a template for states. Where adopted, it caps residential deposits at two months and non-residential deposits at six months. It applies to new tenancies and does not ban leave and licence arrangements.

body.title: Scenario: The Painting Charge Dispute
body.scenario: Deepa rented her Indiranagar, Bengaluru flat for two years on back-to-back 11-month agreements with a ₹2 lakh deposit. At exit, she deducts ₹40,000 for "painting and damages" and refunds ₹1.6 lakh a month later. The tenant says the flat was already scuffed at move-in and the agreement never mentioned painting. He threatens a legal notice and a one-star review on the rental portal.
body.prompt: Where did Deepa go wrong, and how should she handle this now and next time?
body.modelAnswer: She made three mistakes: no painting clause in the agreement, no dated photos or inventory at move-in to prove the condition, and a slow refund with no written breakdown. Now, she should list each deduction with actual quotes or bills, keep what she can prove as damage beyond normal wear and tear, and refund the rest promptly. Two years of normal living will scuff walls, and that is not damage. Fighting over ₹40,000 with weak evidence risks a longer dispute and a reputation that lengthens her next vacancy. Next time, she should add a clear painting and handover clause, record move-in condition with photos and a signed inventory, and commit to a refund timeline, for example within 15 to 30 days of handover.

cards.definition: Permission to use a property without transferring an interest in it, under the Indian Easements Act, 1882.
A transfer of the right to enjoy a property for a term, under the Transfer of Property Act, 1882; must be registered if over one year.
Older state laws that capped rents and restricted eviction, leading to frozen rents on legacy tenancies.
A central template law for states that sets deposit caps, written agreements and fast-track rent dispute forums.
The district-level body under the Model Tenancy Act that records agreements and handles first-level issues.
A signed record of furniture, fittings and their condition at move-in, used to settle deposit deductions at exit.

points: The 11-month leave and licence format exists largely to avoid compulsory registration of leases over one year and the tenant protections of old rent control laws.
Maharashtra requires registration of all leave and licence agreements, and stamp duty applies to rent agreements across states.
A good agreement covers rent, deposit, notice, repairs, inventory, sub-letting and exit condition in writing.
Most deposit disputes are prevented by move-in photos, a signed inventory and a prompt refund with a written breakdown.
The Model Tenancy Act caps residential deposits at two months, sets overstay penalties and creates fast-track rent forums, but only where a state adopts it.
Special cases such as NRI owners and company leases bring extra TDS and documentation requirements.

body.text: Tenancy, stamp duty and registration rules vary by state and change over time. Check your state's current law before signing an agreement, and consult a lawyer for disputes. This lesson is educational and is not legal or tax advice.
